fields.Q1:
WHAT IS STANDING AROUND THIS ROOM MADE OF?**

Large dressed stone blocks — cut ashlar, cool blue-grey, recessed mortar joints, chisel-scratched faces. Roughly 64 screen px (32 logical px at 2× scale) per block.

But I have to be straight with you about how I know that: **I cannot name it at 1:1.** At play size the walls are a black field. I can only name the material after multiplying the image by 14×.
fields.Q1_WHY:
Under gain, the north band (y 198–250), the west column (x 0–56), the east column (x 696–750) and the south band (y 778–825) resolve into large rectangular units with 1-logical-px dark joints, 45° chisel-hatch scratches, a "▽" chamfer notch at the top edge, and a vertical fracture squiggle. The raw mean luminance of that whole ring is **8.2 / 255**.

---
fields.Q2:
SOLID MASS, OR FLAT PATTERN?**

**Solid mass — but only just, and only on one wall.**

The north wall has a genuine three-tier junction. Sampled down the column x=340:
- y 198–229: wall top face, lum 19–22
- y 231–233: hard black leading edge, lum 4–5 (2 logical px)
- y 235–265: darker inner face band, lum 13–18
- y 267+: floor, climbing 26 → 54

That is a real thickness read — top, edge, face, ground. Someone built it deliberately.

The problem is the amplitude. The separation between "top of wall" and "face of wall" is **4–6 levels out of 255**. Sampled across the west wall at y=480 the values run 2, 5, 8, 7, 9, 5 across x=0–110 — no detectable junction at all. So the structure that exists in the file is not the structure that reaches the eye. On screen it is a change of colour.

---
fields.Q3:
WHERE EXACTLY DOES THE GROUND STOP?**

Two transitions, and they behave completely differently.

**Room edge → outside**, at y 197→198 across the full width, and at x 310→311 and x 503→504 at the passage: RGB **(1,1,2) → (6,6,8) in one logical pixel** (2 screen px). No gradient, no cap, no shadow, no dither. The region x 0–300, y 0–196 contains exactly **two unique RGB values** in the entire 58,800 pixels: (1,1,2) and (3,3,4).

**Floor → wall inside the room**, north wall at y≈231: over ~34 screen px, as broken down in Q2. This one is properly constructed and completely invisible.

---
fields.Q4:
WHAT IS HOLDING THIS PLACE TOGETHER?**

**NOTHING.**

No rope, no driven pin, no bracket, no strap, no hide, no timber, no shoring, no wedge, no patch, no brace. I looked for it specifically because the fiction promises it.

The only hard-edged non-masonry objects anywhere in the standing structure are six flat-black rectangles: (187,206) 30×12; (409,782), (531,782), (595,782), (729,782) each 18×12; (213,808) 18×16. They are solid fills — no interior, no fixing, no rim, no shadow. They read as missing pixels, not as hardware.

Four hundred years of an orc company holding this line has left no fixture on it.

---
fields.Q5:
BUILT, OR REPEATED?**

**REPEATED.** Not an impression — pixel arithmetic.

In the south wall band (y 778–824), the 48×46 patch at **x=0 is pixel-for-pixel identical to x=192** (mean absolute difference 0.00, max difference 0). Same for **x=124 ≡ x=252** (128 apart) and **x=504 ≡ x=568** (64 apart). In the west column, **y=264 ≡ y=712** (448 apart = 7×64).

The four black rectangles at y=782 sit at the identical in-cell offset; the surrounding 42×36 patches at x=531 and x=595 are **95.6% pixel-identical, mean diff 0.06, max diff 3**.

Pitch is 64 screen px = 32 logical px. There is real per-tile drawing here — the crack overlays cross joints, the coursing isn't obvious — but the ring is stamped.

---
fields.Q6:
WOULD YOU BELIEVE THIS SHIPPED?**

**YES.** It would ship without comment.

Merely competent. Not genuinely good. There is craft in it — the three-tier junction, the crack lines that cross block boundaries, non-regular coursing — but the ring is stamped from a short tile set, the fiction is entirely absent from it, and none of it reaches the player.

---
fields.Q7:
WHAT CAN YOU ACTUALLY SEE AT 1:1?**

On the standing surfaces: **almost nothing.**

The measurement, over the wall ring:
- mean luminance **8.2/255**; 99th percentile **20**; absolute maximum **34**
- **1.1%** of the ring exceeds lum 20. **0.1%** exceeds 30. **0.0%** exceeds 40.
- Floor, for contrast: 65% above 20, 53% above 30, **31% above 60**.

The brightest pixel on any wall in this frame is darker than the dimmest third of the floor.

Per wall, pixels above lum 25:
- **North band: only x 343–458** — a 115px window directly above the figure.
- **South band: none. Zero pixels.**
- **West column: maximum luminance 20.**
- **East column: maximum luminance 11.**

**Legible at 1:1:** in that north window, faint horizontal coursing and two or three vertical crack squiggles; the black rectangle at (187,206) as a smudge. That is the complete list.

**Only on magnification:** the material itself, the mortar joints, the 45° chisel hatch, the ▽ chamfer, the wall's inner-face band, the black rectangles in the south wall, and every one of the duplications.

**Does it change with distance from the figure?** Barely — because the wall never gets near the light. Figure at (405,487); nearest wall pixel is the north inner edge at (405,~250), r≈237, and the radial profile has already fallen to lum 16 by r=250 and to ambient 7 by r=300. **There is nowhere in this frame where a wall is lit.** The best-lit wall spot is x 380–440, y 245–265 at lum 29–32, against 184 under the figure.
fields.Q7_WHY:
Checked at 1:1: raw crops (0,180)–(750,300); (280,0)–(540,270); (0,380)–(120,620). Had to magnify: (60,190)–(300,320) at 6×; (290,0)–(520,215) at 4× with 6× gain; (140,196)–(260,250) at 8×; (0,778)–(750,824) at 8× with 16× gain; plus a full-frame pass with the radial light profile divided out.

---
fields.Q8:
ANYTHING YOUR EYE KEEPS RETURNING TO?**

Three things.

1. **The vertical crack squiggle.** The same wandering black line, same shape, block after block — down the west column at x≈14–30 for its whole length, and across the north band at roughly 64–96px intervals. It is inside the tile, not authored per location: the pixel-identical patch pairs in Q5 each contain the same squiggle exactly.
2. **The "▽" chamfer** — two diagonals descending to a short vertical bar — at the top edge of block after block along the north band, e.g. (165,200) and (235,200), same in-cell position each time.
3. **Four identical 18×12 black rectangles**, all at exactly y=782, at x = 409, 531, 595, 729.

---
fields.Q9:
WHAT IS BEYOND THE WALLS?**

Nothing. Not more stone, not another room, not darkness with anything in it — the renderer simply stops.

The region x 0–300, y 0–196 contains **two unique colours**: (1,1,2) and (3,3,4). Boosted 40× it stays perfectly blank. There is no fog, no dither margin, no falling-off tone to suggest mass continuing past the cut.

That is a legitimate roguelike convention — unexplored means nothing. But combined with the hard one-pixel cut in Q3, it means the wall reads as the outer edge of a drawing rather than as the near side of something. There is no beyond; there is an end of file.

---
fields.Q10:
COULD YOU TELL A WAY THROUGH FROM A DEAD END?**

I found the gap. Content above y=198 spans x 311–503; within it, **x 375–439** (one 64px tile, centred on the figure's own column at x≈405) is the passage floor, and x 311–375 / x 439–503 are the wall tops flanking it.

**At 1:1 I could not read it as a passage.** It reads as one undifferentiated dark column ~192px wide sticking up out of the room. The passage does not separate from its jambs because they are the same value:

| sample | jamb L | corridor | jamb R |
|---|---|---|---|
| y 200–240 | 17 | 16 | 10 |
| y 150–190 | 6 | 8 | — |

One to two levels of separation. So the honest answer is **no** — you could not tell a way through from a dead end without walking into it.

What made the difference once magnified and normalised was **texture, not value**: the corridor floor is a smoother, finer-grained tile with no block coursing; the jambs carry the big-block chamfer-and-crack pattern. That distinction lives entirely below the visible threshold.

Separately: the passage cuts the wall band as a plain rectangular slot. The blocks at the jamb (x≈360–375, y≈200–230) get no returned face, no darker inner side, no corner treatment. The tile just stops.

---
fields.Q11:
HAS ANYTHING HAPPENED TO THIS STRUCTURE?**

It is cracked. That is the whole condition.

Every wall block carries the same vertical fracture and the same chisel hatching, plus the six black voids. Absent: missing blocks, displaced or tilted coursing, spall, staining, water, soot, accretion, rubble at the base, patch, repair, or any evidence of a boundary that has been contested.

I read that from the uniformity. The damage is identical everywhere, which is the signature of a texture rather than of a history. Nothing has happened *to* this wall — a wear pass was applied *across* it.

---
fields.CULL:
Walls sit at mean luminance 8/255 — invisible at play size — and are stamped from a repeating tile.

---
fields.FLIP LIST:
- Raise the wall ring's unlit floor from mean lum 8/255 (1.1% of pixels above 20) to roughly 28–40, so coursing and the y≈231 joint line read at 1:1; leave the ground's unlit value where it is so the two separate.
- Break the stamping: x=0 is pixel-identical to x=192, x=124 to x=252, x=504 to x=568 in the south band, and y=264 to y=712 in the west column. Author 4–6 variants or apply per-cell offset/flip.
- Remove or redesign the six flat-black rectangles at (187,206), (409/531/595/729, 782) and (213,808) — solid fills with no interior, currently reading as missing pixels.
- Give the passage jambs at x=375 and x=439 (y 198–232) a returned face and a value step, so the opening reads as a gap rather than as a slightly darker stripe in a 192px slab.
- Put the fiction on the wall in at least a few cells per run: rope lashing, driven pins, hide and salvaged timber over the cracks. Nothing in the standing structure is currently holding anything.

---

The single decision that fixes the most here is the value floor. Roughly 90% of what was actually drawn on these walls — the chamfers, the joints, the inner face, the whole three-tier junction — exists in the file and never reaches the screen. Before anyone redraws a tile, find out whether that ambient level is an art choice or a lighting-shader clamp, because if it's the shader you get most of this back for free and the flip list shortens to two items.

*Model: Claude Opus 5 (1M context).*
